entries.d: The Autoloot class allow to interact with the Autoloot Agent, via scripting. The item row Name column can carry a match pattern (all compares case-insensitive): Enter this... Mode Matches "exact name" Exact Only items with exactly that name (leading quantity digits ignored) *glob* Contains Any item whose name contains the pattern (* = any run, ? = one char) /regex/ Regex Items matching the .NET regex, case-insensitive A bare name (no quotes, globs, or slashes) does no name filtering — matching stays purely by ItemID/hue/props. Property filters accept the same pattern syntax on their Name field: *glob* / /regex/ match any property whose rendered line matches, and the min/max range applies to ANY matching property; a bare or "quoted" name stays an exact property lookup (e.g. Dexterity Bonus). The synthetic property Unique Name (any spacing/case) is operator-only: == matches when the item's name differs from its static default name (custom/named items), != matches when it equals the default. Min/Max are ignored.

Example: {'name':'House tiles', 'type':'for', 'fields':[ {'name':'X', 'type':'uint', 'length': 2} {'name':'Y', 'type':'uint', 'length': 2} {'name':'Z', 'type':'uint', 'length': 1} {'name':'staticID', 'type':'modelID'} ] }

entries.d: How far (Chebyshev) the player may be from the nearest tile of a cached road and still use it. Go walks the short hop onto the road from that entrance, so this bounds both the extra planning and the extra walking spent to get back onto a cached route. Beyond it the cache is ignored and a full compute runs. Raise it if your routes start from places the character often ends up a little away from (house doors, rune spots).

How close to the beginning of a cached road counts as "at the start". A player is nearly always placed within a few tiles of where the route began — a rune, a house door, the spot the script walked from — so when they're within this distance of the head of the road the route is entered there and simply walked from the start. Entering at the head keeps the whole road usable, stair zones included; entering at whatever tile happens to be nearest can drop the player halfway into a route whose segments were built for a different start, which is where a long recompute comes from. Only when the player is further than this from the head does the nearest point anywhere on the road get considered, still bounded by .
